rite: He Greek Catholic. She Roman Catholic in 1873 to 1882. In 1857 her rite mark was first read here as Greek Catholic; the Demko agent reads it as Roman Catholic, and on a second look that is the likelier reading.

Burials (B-044): János, aged 2, d. 14 Dec [1872]; the twins Mihály and János, d. 11 and 14 June 1873 at 12 and 15 days; Mihály, one month old, d. 3 May in a year not on the strip, at house 121. A Demko woman married into Senné by 1861.

homes: Solymos; no house numbers in these years
note: The earliest Duska household in the archive. Two daughters named Susanna, eight years apart: the first is presumed to have died (rule 20). Burials (B-048): Susanna d. 8 Nov [1830] aged 1½; Borbála d. 26 Aug [1843]; the mother, Borbála Plyuchta, d. 9 Jan 1847 aged 43; András d. 1 Jun [1873] aged 78 at Solymos 34.

A second Duska couple of the same years as FG-34; János is not the János of 1834, who was seven in 1841. Two sons named János. Commoner in 1852, cottar in 1857. Census of [1869] (D-011-11): János born 1810, Anna born 1820, with sons Mihály (1850) and György (1857). Burials (B-048): János d. 16 Sep [1855] aged 3, of cholera (house 30); the father János d. [Oct 1877] aged 70 (house 33); Anna Hura d. 10 Jun 1880 aged 60; György (b. 1857) d. 20 Oct 1926, his burial naming both parents. A Mihály Dusko, 'son of a farmer with a full holding', d. 25 May 1856 aged 2[9] at house 31; whose son is not stated.
One washed-out entry. A third Duska father of the 1840s.

Either András of FG-34 with a second wife, nine years after his last child by Borbála, or a younger András. A change of mother is a second marriage until a second man is shown (rule 20). House 44 is a Duska house again in 189[3]. Census of [1869] (D-011-12): András Duska, born 1797, and Erzsébet, Roman Catholic, born 1816 at Szenna; the third party reads her surname as Szakács [?]. The György of [1852] is not in the household. A son András, b. about 1850, d. 7 Apr [1854] at Solymos 34, both parents alive (B-048). House 34 is where András the father died in [1873].

wife: Anna Kitko (Kitzka; written Minda once and corrected)

June [1875] at Solymos 33 (B-048): the house of János Duska and Anna Hura, which makes Mihály their son in all likelihood (H-042).
The father may be the György of 1857 (FG-35), of [1852] (FG-37) or of 1847 (FG-36). György d. 7 Mar 1883 at one month (B-048).

Probably this wife; if so, this Mihály died in 1914 (H-069).

Also filed here, without being joined to the couple: Anna, b. 24 Feb [1898], daughter of Mihály Ku[...]s and a Zsuzsánna Duska; and János, b. 15 Apr [1920], illegitimate son of a Zsuzsanna Duska, who may be the Zsuzsanna of [1888] (FG-40). Three women of one name are possible.

husband: András Duska (b. [1868], d. 22 Aug 1940), 'the younger' in 1903

note: Married at Senné on 18 January 1892: András Duska, cottar, 24, son of György Duska and Anna Krak; Anna Nyemcsik, 19, daughter of János Nyemcsik and Erzsébet Hresko (D-006-03). The wife's mother is 'Hresko alias Minarcsin' in her own children's baptisms, which is why the wife is entered as Minarcsin in the 1890s; from 1903 the priest writes Nyemecz. One couple, thirteen children in nineteen years, seven dead in childhood by the notes in the book. Two sets of twins. Their son Mihály, born 3 July 1903, is the leading candidate for Michal Duska, Ahn 8 (H-046). CENSUS OF 1930 (D-011-24): Andrej, born 24 November 1868, and Anna, born 24 August 1872, married 18 January 1892, twelve children, nine living, at house 145 with their son Juraj (1910), their daughter-in-law Maria, born at Iňačovce, and their grandson Štefan, born 23 October 1929. So their son Mihály of 1903 is Michal Duska, Ahn 8, and this couple are Ahn 16 and 17.
